title: Monoidal infinity categories in the nonsymmetric Segal model
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small, and all simplicial sets considered fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use quasicategories, coherent functors and equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the simplex category $\Delta$ from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and cocartesian fibrations and fibers from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Regard $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ as its nerve. A morphism $[n]\to[m]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is inert if its opposite $[m]\to[n]$ is $j\mapsto a+j$ for some $a$; put $\rho_i:[n]\to[1]$ for the opposite of $j\mapsto i-1+j$, $1\leq i\leq n$.

A monoidal infinity category in the nonsymmetric model is a cocartesian fibration $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ for which the transport maps along the $\rho_i$ induce equivalences $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}\to(\mathcal V^\otimes_{[1]})^n$ for every $n\geq0$. Here the product is the degreewise product of quasicategories and the zeroth product is the one-point quasicategory; write $\mathcal V=\mathcal V^\otimes_{[1]}$. Cocartesian transport along the opposite of $[1]\to[n]$, $0\mapsto0$, $1\mapsto n$, is the $n$-fold tensor functor under these Segal identifications; for $n=0$ it specifies the tensor unit $\mathbf1$ up to equivalence. An edge of $\mathcal V^\otimes$ is inert if it is $p$-cocartesian and lies over an inert base map. A lax monoidal functor is a coherent functor over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving inert edges; a strong monoidal functor preserves all cocartesian edges.

source.place: Gepner-Haugseng, Definitions 3.1.1, 3.1.3, 3.1.10, 3.1.15, 3.1.17 and 3.1.20 (lax and strong monoidal functors); the Segal cocartesian-fibration formulation is the monoidal specialization. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag defines this infinity-categorical notion.
